_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Coromandel International (consolidated, ₹ crore). Segment-driven: Nutrient & allied and Crop protection each grow revenue and earn an EBITDA margin (segment PBIT + segment D&A, excluding impairments). A third line removes inter-segment sales. Group EBITDA = sum of segments less central costs (Screener basis, excluding other income). Valued on P/E, as the street does. Engine workaround: the tax line also carries minorities and a share-count true-up (see _taxWhy).

segments.name: Nutrient & allied
segments._why: FY27: Q1 revenue +9% (prices up 25-30% across grades, DAP+NPK volumes -9% as production was cut to 72% utilisation); rabi demand at risk after a monsoon at 87% of normal (south peninsula 76%) and low southern reservoirs, and imported DAP limited: +10%. FY28 +8%: the 7.5 lakh t granulation train (commissioning Q4FY27) adds volume while prices ease if Middle East supply normalises. FY29 +7%: volume growth from the expanded Kakinada complex and SSP/specialty nutrients.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 14.1% (FY20), 14.8% (FY21), 11.4% (FY22), 10.1% (FY23), 11.8% (FY24), 11.5% (FY25), 10.8% (FY26). Q1FY27 PBIT margin 6.9% vs 9.9% a year earlier as ammonia, sulphur and phosphoric acid ($1,700/t for Q2 vs $1,360) outran a 10% NBS increase. FY27 9.2% assumes only partial relief in H2. FY28 11.0% and FY29 11.2%: own sulphuric/phosphoric acid (60% of needs), Senegal rock and granulation volumes lift EBITDA/t towards ~₹5,500-6,000 (management target ₹6,500), but subsidy policy and reasonable-margin guidelines cap the upside: still below FY24-25 margins on today's higher price base.

segments.name: Crop protection
segments._why: FY27 +30%: a full year of NACL (consolidated from 8-Aug-2025; FY26 NACL revenue ₹1,585 cr, of which ₹923 cr consolidated) plus standalone growth of ~18% (Q1 +20%; guidance 20-25%; 20,000 t mancozeb expansion at Sarigam). FY28 +14% (standalone ~17%, NACL ~5%); FY29 +12%.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 15.3-18.7% (FY20-21), 14.0-16.5% (FY22-25), 14.8% in FY26 with NACL's low-margin months and acquisition amortisation-free EBITDA. Standalone PBIT margin ~19% (FY26) and 18% in Q1FY27; NACL EBITDA margin 11% in Q1FY27 ('reasonable level' without new products). Mix-weighted 15.5% / 16.0% / 16.5% as NACL slowly improves.

segments.name: Inter-segment eliminations
segments._why: Sales between the segments removed on consolidation: ₹174 cr (FY24), ₹204 cr (FY25), ₹216 cr (FY26); we assume +10% a year.
segments._marginWhy: Inter-segment profit adjustment has been within ±₹6 cr a year: modelled at zero.

_unallocLabel: Central costs not allocated to segments (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
_unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: ₹310 cr (FY24), ₹335 cr (FY25), ₹343 cr (FY26); reported unallocable expense ₹291 cr / ₹283 cr / ₹359 cr. We assume ₹360-400 cr as corporate, R&D and retail-network costs grow.
_capexWhy: FY26 cash capex ₹1,540 cr (Kakinada acid plants). FY27 ₹900 cr = capital commitments of ₹619 cr at Mar-2026 (granulation, T-MAP, mancozeb, fluorination launch plant) plus ~₹300 cr of maintenance; FY28-29 ₹600 cr = management's 'normal sustainable capex of ₹300 crores' for Coromandel plus NACL, Senegal and retail-store spending.
_depWhy: FY26 D&A ₹534 cr = 6.8% of average gross block, but Q1FY27 D&A was ₹203 cr (₹812 cr annualised) as the acid plants (+₹16-18 cr a quarter), NACL acquisition intangibles (~₹21 cr) and Senegal mine overburden (~₹30 cr) came in. 7.8% gives ~₹760 cr / ~₹820 cr / ~₹870 cr for FY27-29.
_treasuryWhy: Net treasury at Mar-2026: cash ₹494 cr + investments ₹2,044 cr + ICDs with Bajaj Finance ₹1,564 cr (6.8-8.2%) less borrowings incl. leases ₹1,506 cr = ₹2,596 cr. 6.5% on the opening balance, below the deposit rate because seasonal working capital (subsidy receivables peak in Q2) absorbs part of the cash during the year.
_otherIncomeWhy: Other income ₹240 cr in FY26 (Screener, normal) and ₹50 cr in Q1FY27 as the cash pile fell after the NACL purchase and capex; ~₹30 cr a year of non-treasury items on top of the treasury yield (FY27E total ~₹200 cr).

otherTreasury.label: Inter-corporate deposits with Bajaj Finance (in other assets)
otherTreasury._why: ICDs of ₹1,564 cr placed with Bajaj Finance at 6.8-8.2% sit in 'loans' (other assets) on Screener; the company itself counts them as cash in its net-debt calculation (note 32.1).

_interestWhy: FY26 ₹343 cr; Q1FY27 ₹89 cr (₹68 cr a year earlier). Most of it is the cost of acceptances and working-capital lines that fund imported raw materials, which cost more at today's prices: ₹400 cr in FY27, easing to ₹370 cr as prices normalise.
_taxWhy: Underlying tax rate 26% (FY26 27.5% incl. the non-deductible drone impairment; Q1FY27 26%; statutory 25.17% plus subsidiaries' losses without tax credit). Engine workaround: the model has no minority-interest line and takes its share count from FY26 total profit ÷ EPS (₹1,898 cr ÷ ₹66.31 = 28.62 cr shares vs 29.50 cr actual diluted shares, because FY26 profit attributable to owners, ₹1,956 cr, exceeded total profit as minorities absorbed ₹58 cr of losses). So the 'tax' line here = 1 − (28.62 ÷ 29.50) × (1 − 26%) + minorities' share of profit (₹0 / ₹10 / ₹20 cr in FY27-29E). Model EPS then equals profit attributable to owners ÷ 29.50 cr shares; model 'net profit' is that profit × 0.97.
_payoutWhy: FY26 dividend ₹11 a share (interim ₹9 + final ₹2) = 17% of EPS; FY25 payout ~11-21%. We assume 18%.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash and essential, policy-supported demand, but earnings swing with subsidy rates, imported raw materials and the monsoon: slightly below market risk.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian fertiliser and crop-protection demand grows with farm output and prices; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Phosphatic demand grows ~3-4% in volume plus price; crop protection faster: 8% by year 12.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Group EBITDA margin was 10.3-11.3% in FY22-26 (14% in FY21): 11% long-run, as subsidy policy caps fertiliser returns.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 2.5% of revenue long-run (FY22-25 average ~2.6%), above depreciation at 2.0% to fund volume growth.
dcf._yearsWhy: 12-year explicit/fade period: the business is mature and net-cash, so no project J-curve to accommodate.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The government compensates the Middle East cost spike in the rabi NBS rates, raw-material prices normalise, own acid and Senegal rock lift fertiliser EBITDA towards ₹6,500/t, and crop protection compounds at 20%+.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Rabi subsidy rates stay inadequate while sulphur and ammonia stay high; a weak southern rabi after the 2026 monsoon cuts volumes; reasonable-margin guidelines cap fertiliser profits; NACL stalls.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Coromandel: Motilal Oswal 25x FY28E EPS (Jul-2026); earlier Sharekhan 26x FY28E and Nuvama 30x Q2FY28E (Dec-2025). 15x = the stock's 17.5x one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 cut by the ~14% de-rating of Indian fertiliser and agrochemical stocks at 30-Sep-2026. Bull 19x (its five-year median trailing P/E: no de-rating, the market keeps paying for the agri-solutions story); bear 12x (the 2021 level, a plain fertiliser maker under subsidy stress).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Values the business and the ~₹6,400 cr of Sep-28E net cash separately. 9x = the stock's 11.8x five-year median trailing EV/EBITDA less the ~22% EV/EBITDA de-rating of the same peers; it does not charge the step-up in depreciation (Senegal mine, NACL intangibles, acid plants).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: FCFF FY28-FY38E fading to an 11% EBITDA margin and capex at 2.5% of revenue, Ke 11.9% (beta 0.9), terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
